appSubtitle: From grid cell to delivery plan

vocabulary.meaning: RSM's full map of the kinds of service operator a client could be. Rendered as the grid.
The TOM for field service: service motivation (rows) by service scenario (columns).
Everything a cell pre-loads: jobs to be done, KPIs, question set, baseline process. The TOM is the map; the blueprint is the pin.
A client request that leaves the cell's baseline.
Customization, Report, Integration, or Modification created by an off-blueprint request.

tour.title: Place the client on the grid
tour.talkTrack: A short set of plain-language questions puts Meridian in one cell. The scoring stays behind the curtain; the associate only sees the answers and the result.

tour.title: Jobs to be done, tiered
tour.talkTrack: The cell hands delivery a tiered backlog on day one. Go-live scope is already argued for.

tour.title: KPIs for this cell
tour.talkTrack: The measures that matter for a profit-center equipment operator. A cost-center appointment operator gets a different list.

tour.title: The question set
tour.talkTrack: This is what an associate takes onto the call: the question, why we ask it, what good sounds like, and what a red flag signals.

tour.title: Baseline process
tour.talkTrack: The standard work-order lifecycle for this cell. Every later request is measured against this line.

tour.title: Make the cost of deviation visible
tour.talkTrack: Each off-blueprint request shows what it creates and what it costs to carry. Accept them all and watch the risk climb.

tour.title: Why this is more efficient
tour.talkTrack: Discovery effort moves to the deltas, the pyramid widens at the base, and every engagement sharpens the cell for the next one.
